changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/5926-empty-action-visible-when.md`

- names `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` → `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `visibleWhen` is not a per-block concern in this platform. It is enforced **once, generically**, in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`: `shouldHide` tests `visibleWhen` ahead of the hoisted `visible` (objectui#5454), sets `_hidden`, and the `_hidden` early return fires **before** the registry dispatches. A block renderer cannot ignore the gate, because it never sees the node.

### `.changeset/7319-dead-schemarenderer-retired.md`

- names `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` → `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `packages/components/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` was a 28-line component carrying the same export name as the real renderer in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`. Nothing reached it: it is absent from the package barrel, no file in the repo imports it by any form, and the package's `exports` map has no subpath that resolves to it.

### `.changeset/7415-action-type-input-rename.md`

- names `SchemaRenderer.tsx` → `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Census of the authored corpus, measured before the rename, not assumed.** Across 4,797 files in `examples/`, `apps/console/`, `content/docs/` and `packages/`: **zero** authored nodes set the input. 517 JSON files (433 of them the schema catalog) contain 2,410 `type`-bearing nodes and **no** `action:button` / `action:icon` node at all — control: 127 plain `button` nodes on the same walk. 207 parsed fenced JSON blocks in md/mdx carry **5** `action:button` nodes, all of them `{ type, label, icon?, action }` — the discriminator plus the `action` channel, none setting an execution type — control: 28 plain `button` nodes, and the count independently matches the corpus census already recorded in `SchemaRenderer.tsx` ("`action:button` (5 nodes)"). No docs page documents the input; no catalog entry uses the components. So the rename breaks no authored document in this repo.

### `.changeset/9959-refused-data-prop-warn-reset.md`

- names `SchemaRenderer.tsx` → `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > The dedupe `Set` behind the objectui#9571 / objectui#9758 diagnostic — "the authored `data` key was NOT passed to the component as a React prop" — lived in `SchemaRenderer.tsx` with nothing able to clear it, while every other dev diagnostic in this package's `utils/` directory pairs its `Set` with an exported test-only reset. `propsBagDiagnostic.ts` states the consequence in its own reset's docblock: the second test to assert the same warning reads the first test's dedupe entry and sees silence, "a green run that checked nothing". The absence direction is the dangerous one — a test asserting this warning did NOT fire for a `type#id` an earlier test already warned for is green whatever the renderer does, and it reports that green as coverage.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `1a88ce22f` (merge-base with origin/main): 7 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1919 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2537 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36847918658)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e22274398163ec26edfa2a562e9d70955b4bc0af`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-01T10:32Z by the isolated at-tier reviewer running inside the `domain:spec @ objectui` seat's session, on PR #11374 for card #11349 (objectui#8347's react preparation unit).

**Inputs, and nothing else:** card #11349's body and its three comments (claim `5926819465`, os-dev-report `5929366107`, seat ACCEPT `5929396272`); PR #11374's body, its 8-file list and the net diff against `main` (merge-base `d0fba91aa`, 8 files, +235 / −33); the check-runs on the head (42 at first read, 43 once the `Test` rollup appeared; read last, as the brief orders). Files at the head were read with `git show` at the sha, never checked out; the spec rows were read at objectstack `0f6dcac5e9` (the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0). Governing texts: AGENTS.md §5 #0.1, the objectui#7927 ruling `5565351677`, the seat's Q2 ruling on the card body, and the maintainer's 2026-08-18 `props` ruling as quoted at `propsWithoutCanonicalKeys`. The dev's report, the seat's ACCEPT and the PR body were read as claims. Nothing was built, run or re-run: the P1-mutation 0/0, the 70/70 `.d.ts` sha256 comparison and proof legs A/B stay the dev's claims, each judged below for consistency with the diff only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface: no exported symbol changes — RIGHT, premise holds on the diff.** `SchemaRenderer.tsx` exports exactly four symbols at the head (`evaluateConfigBagInScope`, `SchemaErrorBoundary`, `SchemaRendererProps`, `SchemaRenderer`) and the diff touches none of their declarations: `SchemaRenderer` keeps its explicit `ForwardRefExoticComponent` annotation and `evaluateConfigBagInScope` is declared `(bag: unknown, …): unknown`. `DeclaredMembersOf`, `InterpreterMarkers`, `WorkingCopyAuthoredKeys` and `InterpreterWorkingCopy` are declared without `export` and are referenced only by the non-exported `resolveAriaProps` and the memo's local `newSchema`; `packages/react/src/index.ts` star-exports the module, so only the four reach the package face. The one new import is `type PageComponent` (type-only). The dev's "70/70 byte-identical `.d.ts`" is a claim, and it is the claim this diff predicts.
- **Accept set: unchanged — RIGHT.** `SchemaRendererProps.schema` stays `BaseSchema | string | null | undefined`; `packages/types/src/base.ts` is not in the diff, so `BaseSchema` keeps every member and its index signature. The prohibition holds: nothing declared on `BaseSchema`; no `any` kept for the copy; no read cast to `any` (the diff adds no `any` token outside comments and removes the `Record`-of-`any` parameter).
- **The working type matches the ruling — RIGHT.** Part 1, `DeclaredMembersOf` applied to `BaseSchema`: a key-remapping mapped type that drops the `string` / `number` / `symbol` index keys and keeps each declared member with its modifiers (`body?: never` included); the identity once objectui#8347 lands. Part 2, `InterpreterMarkers`, with the docblock saying the memo writes them: confirmed at the head — written only at `shouldHide` (`newSchema._hidden = true`) and the enablement chain (`newSchema._disabled = true`); read only at `if (evaluatedSchema._hidden) return null` and the metadata destructure, which strips both and re-emits `disabled: __disabled || undefined`. Part 4, the string-keyed `unknown` record. Part 3, `WorkingCopyAuthoredKeys`, is the ruling's own `props` instruction ("type it on the working type as that annotated alias", `unknown`) plus `visibility`; naming `visibility` on the copy is the per-key rule's "the spec declares the key: read it through the declared type", applied at the declaration because the read site has no narrowing guard (the leg is `!== undefined` then `evaluateVisibilityPredicate`), so an `unknown` there would have forced a cast or a new guard, i.e. a verdict change. Internal and non-exported: option (b) as ruled.
- **The `visibility` reference — RIGHT.** At objectstack `0f6dcac5e9`, `packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts` declares on `PageComponentSchema`: `/** @deprecated ADR-0089 — use visibleWhen. Accepted and normalized to visibleWhen at parse. */ visibility: EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema.optional()`, the whole shape ending `.transform(normalizeVisibleWhen)`; `export type PageComponent = z.input` of that schema, re-exported from `/ui` by `export * from './page.zod'`. The INPUT face is the correct one: the renderer reads raw, un-normalized metadata, and the parsed face is what `normalizeVisibleWhen` has already folded. The type is the same `EvaluatedExpressionInput` the spec gives `visibleWhen`. `BaseSchema` declares `visible`, `visibleWhen`, `visibleOn`, `hidden`, `hiddenOn` but not `visibility`, so the intersection carries no conflict. The row is `@deprecated`; the deprecation's end stays the spec's (③ below).
- **Per-key verdicts: none retires, none declares; every named guard exists at the head and guards the read it is credited with — RIGHT.**
  - `properties` (declared: spec `PageComponentSchema.properties`, `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`): the raw-bag snapshot and the hoist both sit behind `isConfigBag(newSchema.properties)` (`utils/configBag.ts`, a `value is` guard to a string-keyed `unknown` record: the spec's declared type exactly). The hoist's dynamic write `newSchema[k] = v` goes through the record part.
  - `props` (bound by the 2026-08-18 ruling, objectui#5123, quoted at `propsWithoutCanonicalKeys`): `unknown` on the working type; the evaluation read is behind `isConfigBag(newSchema.props)`; the alias handoff is `propsWithoutCanonicalKeys(propsBag: unknown, propertiesBag: unknown)`. Not retired, not widened.
  - `params` (declared: spec `ActionButtonPropsSchema.params` / `ActionIconPropsSchema.params`, `z.unknown().optional()`): `isParamsBag(newSchema[PARAMS_KEY])` (`utils/paramsBag.ts`, a `value is` guard) guards the one read-then-write.
  - text keys (declared by the spec's carriage map `EXPRESSION_BINDABLE_TEXT_KEYS_BY_COMPONENT`: `statistic` → label / value / description, `card` → title / description, `button` → label): the loop reads `newSchema[key]` once into `authoredText`, `typeof authoredText === 'string'` narrows it, and the write is the same `evaluator.evaluate(…)`.
  - `content` (declared: spec `ElementTextPropsSchema.content`; objectui `TextSchema.content`): `typeof newSchema.content === 'string'`, an unchanged line.
  - `responsiveStyles` (declared: spec `PageComponentSchema.responsiveStyles: ResponsiveStylesSchema.optional()`): `hasResponsiveStyles` (`@object-ui/core` `scoped-styles.ts`, `rs is ResponsiveStyles`, the spec-owned type) guards the one read; the `node as Record` cast is gone.
  - `objectFields`, `schema`, `dataSource`: destructure-and-discard strips (`schema: _schema`, `dataSource: _dataSource`, `objectFields: _objectFields`), read as `unknown`, nothing forwarded. `objectFields` is a host runtime prop (batch #70, objectui#7742; objectui#8818 closes the key here); `schema` protects the component's own `schema` prop seat; `dataSource` is declared by the spec and its verdict is objectui#11070's per the card's Serial. Nothing retired, nothing declared, so no retirement census is owed in this PR; the PR body's producer census is a dated observation this record does not rest on.
- **Runtime: no behaviour change — RIGHT, every non-type line judged.** (i) `const newSchema: InterpreterWorkingCopy = { ...schema }`: annotation only. (ii) The text-key loop now reads the key once into a local before the same `typeof` test and the same write; nothing writes `newSchema` between the old read and the old re-read, so the value evaluated and the value assigned are the ones the old code took. (iii) `resolveAriaProps`: the parameter goes from a `Record` of `any` to `InterpreterWorkingCopy` and the return from `Record` of `string | undefined` to `Record` of `unknown`; the body is byte-for-byte the same three `if` blocks, so `aria-label` is still `resolveKeyedI18nLabel(schema.ariaLabel)` (a `BaseSchema` member) and `aria-describedby` / `role` are forwarded as authored; the result is only ever spread into `createElement`, whose props are `ForwardedProps`. The old `string | undefined` return was never true of an `any` input. (iv) `scopedStyling`: a cast removed, same JS. The tests' identity helpers return their argument unchanged.
- **Tests: no assertion weakened — RIGHT.** Six suites type their literals through identity helpers (`flatAriaProbe` = `BaseSchema` with `Pick` of the spec's `AriaProps` for `ariaDescribedBy` / `role`; `stableWidget`; `deprecatedVisibilityNode` = `BaseSchema` with `Pick` of `PageComponent` for `visibility`; `scopedStyleNode` for `responsiveStyles`; `textKeyProbeNode`; and `TextSchema` for the reconciliation fixture). Each literal stays a FRESH literal passed to a typed parameter, so excess-property checking survives objectui#8347's removal, which is what the helpers are for. Not one `expect` line is in the diff: the `visibility` alias case still asserts `container.innerHTML` is `''`, the aria cases still assert the three attributes. The reconciliation fixture `{ type: 'text', value: 'Hello' }` → `const textNode: TextSchema = { type: 'text', content: 'Hello' }` assigned to `CoreSchemaNode`: `TextSchema.value` is a `never` tombstone (objectui#7016), so the old spelling authored a retired key through the index signature; the pin "an object is a node through core's name" is kept and now also checks `TextSchema` against the union. Same string. The two cross-file `path:line` citations (`SchemaRenderer.tsx:111`, `:466`) are re-cited by content (AGENTS.md §5 #11); the diff adds no new line citation.
